hypothesis: A reversible upstream-inspired block-deletion search can overcome the irreversible compatibility bottleneck and assemble more than four mutually compatible rows at scope <=111 in pure Python.
rationale: The pinned upstream dts-search-hdl algorithm repeatedly deletes an earlier block when the next block cannot be generated, then tries a replacement against the remaining cumulative spectrum. This is a materially different search policy from irreversible random greedy selection and the fixed-row pool search, while preserving exact bitmask compatibility checks.
expected_information_gain: Measures whether reversible block deletion increases assembled row depth or unique differences, and whether any complete assignment survives independent DTS validation; a negative result tests the remaining pure-Python search family before pausing active DTS compute.
method: Generate six-mark rows sequentially using exact integer difference bitmasks and a published-witness-derived mark-position profile. When a row cannot be generated within the mark-attempt cap, delete earlier rows in randomized order and try a replacement against the rebuilt cumulative spectrum; if all replacements fail, back off one row and continue. Run independent fixed seeds and validate any complete assignment with verify_dts.verify.
metric: deepest assembled row count, unique positive differences, deletion/replacement counts, and complete independent DTS validity under scope <=111
metric_relation_to_true_objective: Only a validator-accepted seven-row assignment with scope <=111 is true-objective progress; row depth and unique-difference counts are Level 1 search proxies.

configuration.profile_source: published scope-112 witness embedded as search distribution only
configuration.upstream_inspiration: dts-search-hdl block deletion and cumulative-spectrum bitmasks

kill_condition: Stop after three 20-second seeded runs or immediately on an independently validated scope-111 witness.

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement is diagnostic unless validator-valid

interpretation: The reversible block-deletion policy improved the diagnostic assembly depth to five rows and 75 unique differences for every seed, versus the prior four-row/60-difference greedy result, but no run completed seven rows and no target witness was independently validated.
what_was_learned: Deletion and replacement materially improve partial assembly depth over irreversible greedy selection, but the tested pure-Python generator still failed before a complete seven-row assignment. The proxy gain does not establish a scope-111 DTS.
recommended_next_action: Pause active DTS search. Resume only after a Linux-compatible exact solver/runtime or a materially new candidate representation is available; preserve this reversible-search result as diagnostic evidence.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of irreversible random greedy or sampled-pool DFS: it changes the state transition policy by deleting and replacing earlier rows while using sequential exact bitmask generation inspired by the pinned upstream search.
